02 Projects & ventures

IDEAS INTO WORKING SOFTWARE

Return to Code

An independent, self-paced study platform for engineers refreshing coding and system design. Choose TypeScript or Python for DSA practice with 190 linked LeetCode problems, or study System Design through worked cases and diagram-and-text exercises. Each course includes concept checks, references, videos, notes, and private progress synced across devices through Google sign-in.

Explore courses ↗

Alma & Jaime Jewelry

As a side hobby, I launched and operate the online store for Alma & Jaime Jewelry, our family jewelry business based in Atlanta, Georgia, and established in 2001. I’m continuing to work on its growth, including exploring an expansion to Seattle.

Explore project

Sage

A chief-of-staff plugin for Claude Code that coordinates specialist agents through design, implementation, review, and verification, with a persistent logbook and optional autopilot. A separate Codex plugin shares the principles, writing guides, and manual logbook tools; Sage mode and autopilot remain Claude-only.

Explore project

sage-bot

A Discord window into Sage across multiple projects. Teams can check task boards, inspect task details, browse shared files, and answer product questions in dedicated threads. Role-based access and an audit trail keep the owner in control. Tested with simulated Discord; a live trial is still pending.

Explore project

Orchestrator

A local workspace for designing software with a lead agent, then coordinating Claude and Codex teams to build it. Editable workflows, isolated Git worktrees, and versioned artifacts keep the work visible. Includes a simulated demo that needs no API keys.

Explore project

Order Chaser

An experiment in agent-built software: a local Kraken order simulator using live public prices. It models spot and margin orders, price caps, partial fills, and recovery from disconnected feeds, with a persistent simulated account. Dry-run only: no API keys or live trades.

Explore project

SaiunCLI

A Python framework for prettier, customizable command-line tools.

Explore project

TextAnalysis

A paired case study comparing New York Times reporting on Alexei Navalny and Julian Assange. Built for a philosophy paper to explore quantitative patterns in coverage.

Explore project

Junior Design App

IVIE, a persuasion analysis dashboard for Reddit discussions. Combines machine learning to detect persuasive text with heuristic scoring for ethos, logos, and pathos, then visualizes the results.

Explore project

VentoyUSB

A multiboot USB setup utility for Windows, macOS, and Linux. Native PowerShell and Bash workflows guide disk selection and verify ISO copies with SHA-256. On macOS, Mactoy handles Ventoy installation; the utility handles copying and verification.

Explore project

I really loved reading this. It’s a short read - only a few minutes but it feels like a hug. A really cool idea for what God and human life is about. 👍

A Short Stay in Hell

Steven L. Peck

About this book ↗
My review

I really enjoyed the book. It was a quick read for an afternoon with an interesting premise. I liked the pacing and subplots but wish there was a happier ending. I was left a bit confused on what this hell was trying to teach its guests. My takeaway is that this is something about human nature and searching and hope. This hell had many emergent qualities of life on Earth. I guess humans will always be human no matter their environment. They will love and grieve and play - form groups and spend their time solving problems and searching for something. On Earth, like in Hell, we hope that someone or something whether it be God or something else can witness and validate our struggles and efforts.
